7484.t: Traditionally derived from κνίζω (knízō, “scratch or gash”); yet the -ι- is long in this word, which may point to Pre-Greek origin, according to Beekes.

7497.t: Perhaps related to κόρυς (kórŭs, “helmet”), referring to the thick end of the weapon. According to Beekes, the word is of Pre-Greek origin.

7476.t: From the root of κλίνω (klī́nō, “to lie down; to recline”).

7457.t: The connection with καῖρος (kaîros, “string”) seems obvious. The presence of the alternative forms leads to a Pre-Greek origin.

7472.t: According to Beekes, from Pre-Greek. Furnée compares κιθάρα (kĭthắrā, “ivy”).

7485.t: Based on the stem forms κνιδ-, κνισ- (knid-, knis-), likely from a Proto-Indo-European *kneyd- (“to scratch, knock”), from *ken- (“to scratch; scrape; rub”).

7496.t: An iterative deverbative verb, lacking a good etymology.

7432.t: Form κατα- (kata-, “intensifying prefix”) + οἰκοδομέω (oikodoméō, “build”), equivalent to κατα- (kata-) + οἰκοδόμος (oikodómos) + -έω (-éō).
